grade.summary: The submitted solution completely proves both claims. The lexicographically decreasing pair (N,S) establishes finite termination and, together with preservation of at least one entry greater than 1, yields the required terminal state. Primewise, the gcd of all valuations is correctly shown to be invariant under the Euclidean transformation (a,b)↦(min(a,b),|a−b|), which uniquely reconstructs the terminal integer M from the initial board.
strengths: The termination measure is valid and every possible case of a move is handled correctly.
The proof correctly establishes that at least one entry remains greater than 1, so a terminal board has exactly one such entry.
The prime-valuation transformation and gcd invariance are correctly derived.
The terminal prime factorization formula uniquely determines M from the initial entries.
